mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 3.0%) reduces the cost of capital and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate sustained monetary easing.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 4.0%) signals economic distress and potential policy stimulus, generating positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns as investors anticipate fiscal interventions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO > 102.0) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.8) signals strengthening labor market conditions, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO > 102.0 and UNRATE < 3.8.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a decline in CPIAUCSL reduces inflation risk and stabilizes interest rate expectations, generating positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles when CPIAUCSL declines.

mechanism_narrative: A high housing starts level (HOUST > 1600.0) signals robust consumer confidence and construction activity, producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns through momentum-driven market participation.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1600.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO > 102.0) and housing starts (HOUST > 1550.0) signals integrated economic expansion across manufacturing and construction, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO > 102.0 and HOUST > 1550.0.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in employment (PAYEMS < 157000.0) signals labor market contraction and recessionary risk, generating negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors price in policy uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 157000.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, high retail sales (RSAFS > 700000.0) signals sustained consumer spending momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns through continued economic confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances during late-cycle expansions when RSAFS > 700000.0.
